children: TOKYO--Consumer inflation in Tokyo remained above the Bank of Japan's 2% target in October, adding to market speculation that the central bank will deliver another interest-rate increase before year-end.

Closely watched as a leading indicator of nationwide trends, the figures come on the cusp of the BOJ's policy decision. While the central bank is widely expected to hold rates steady Friday, many forecasters are penciling in hikes in the months ahead.

Friday's inflation print suggests there is room to tighten. Excluding fresh food, consumer prices in the Tokyo metropolitan area rose 2.6% in October from a year earlier, compared with a 2.7% gain in September. That matched the forecast in a poll of economists by data provider Quick.
The BOJ raised its policy rate to 1.25% in September, pushing borrowing costs to a three-decade high as board members grew increasingly alert to upside price risks.

The conflict in the Middle East, a weak yen, and demand spillovers from the artificial-intelligence boom all pose risks to Japan's price outlook. When it unveils its policy decision later, the central bank will release fresh projections that will show how it expects growth and inflation to develop.
Reflecting concerns that inflation could overshoot the 2% target, markets are now pricing in about an 80% chance of another interest-rate increase at the BOJ's final meeting of the year in December.
